text:
nina: Vendor-constellation alerted: H100 EU ETA slipped from ~7d -> ~15d due to customs sampling + a depot quarantine backlog. This will squeeze Dedicated EU capacity for the tenant rollout next week.

vendor-constellation: Confirmed. Root cause: random customs sampling on a subset of containers + one depot triage lane closed for sanitation. Options we can execute: (A) airbridge consolidation of up to 12 units (ETA 48-72h) at +$2,200/unit; (B) full ocean (32 units) ETA 12-16d no surcharge; (C) origin pre-burn-in & inspection (48h at origin) at $150/unit which reduces observed depot fail-rate from ~0.6% -> ~0.15% and lets you accept sea without spares; (D) temporary loaner pool (10 units) staged in FRA for 7-10d @ $600/unit handling. We can also preprint RMA return labels and include crate-level NFC stickers if amendment signed.

maya: Please upload updated ETA matrix, serial manifest CSV, sample pre-burn-in report template, and RMA label spec. We also need the insurance certificate (cargo all-risks) and the broker contact for customs escalation.

vendor-constellation: Will upload manifest+docs in 2h. RMA label format: CONST_{depot}_{po}_{serial}. Pre-burn-in report template attached will include test_pass (Y/N), voltage_smoke test, and photo_md5. Carrier insurance cert and customs broker contact included. Note: origin pre-burn-in consumes 48h on our dock but removes need for additional spares in most waves.

sam: Quick back-of-envelope: airbridge 12 * 2200 = 26,400. Origin pre-burn-in for 32 units = 32 * 150 = 4,800. Loaners 10 * 600 = 6,000. If launch needs +30 GPUs by D+6 and EU slack = 11, airbridge seems safer but expensive. Pre-burn-in might let us accept ocean and still be ok if fail-rate is low.

```
air_cost = 12 * 2200 = 26400
preburn_cost = 32 * 150 = 4800
loaner_cost = 10 * 600 = 6000
```

sam: If we can tolerate 12d sea, pre-burn-in + no spares saves a lot. But timeline risk is the gating factor.

eli: Ops note: pre-burn-in report plus NFC crate tags would allow our depot to auto-validate incoming crates and waive the 24h photo SLA for those crates, speeding intake. But we need the origin test logs as CSV/sha256 to verify. Also confirm whether pre-burn-in includes full burn-in (48h) or a smoke test.

vendor-constellation: Pre-burn-in = 48h continuous burn-in including power cycle and stress test; report includes per-serial pass/fail, temperature logs (sample), and photos with photo_md5. We'll provide manifest.sha256 and per-serial test_report.csv. Crate NFC payload = {po,crate_id,manifest_sha256}.

maya: Good. Requirements we need in the PO amendment: 1) manifest CSV schema = serial, sku, shipped_ts, depot_id, crate_id, test_pass, photo_md5, manifest_sha256; 2) if pre-burn-in chosen, vendor must attach test_report.csv and manifest.sha256; 3) RMA labels in-box; 4) security: vendor must provide insurer cert and broker contact; 5) depot intake: if origin pre-burn-in provided and sha256 matches, depot photo SLA relaxed to 48h, else 24h.

ops-eu: Confirm we can implement relaxed SLA only if manifest.sha256 verified and crate NFC scanned on arrival. Otherwise enforce 24h photo requirement and RMA pickup <=72h. Also request vendor to include a crate-level QR with manifest link for quick ingestion.

nina: Priority = launch. @procurement-bot please draft PO amendment with two parallel options: (1) origin pre-burn-in + full ocean (preferred cost path), (2) airbridge 12 units if procurement & finance approve expedite. Include spare policy as optional: vendor will provide 1 spare per 100 at no extra freight if amendment signed. Flag finance for one-off expedite spend on option (2).

procurement-bot: PO 90444_amendment draft created with two options (pre-burn-in+ocean fallback and airbridge expedite). Tagging @finance and procurement-team for approval.

finance: Preliminary OK on pre-burn-in path. One-off expedite for airbridge requires full justification; tentative cap $30k under code 4410. Procure to finalize and provide cost allocation.

sam: I recommend we try pre-burn-in first (low cost) and only trigger airbridge if manifest ingestion or customs escalations fail. Approve pre-burn-in path now. Procurement to finalize amendment including insurance verification and manifest.sha256 check.

maya: Agreed. We'll ingest test_report.csv into manifest pipeline and verify sha256 before permitting depot SLA relaxation. ops-eu to ready NFC+QR intake workflow.

vendor-constellation: Understood. We'll begin pre-burn-in for the ocean lots immediately and upload test_report.csv + manifest.sha256 within 48h. Airbridge hold will remain on standby pending PO amendment signature. We'll include printed RMA labels and crate NFC stickers for origin-tested crates.

ops-eu: We'll stand up the NFC ingestion endpoint and pre-register crate_ids in the depot system. Please ensure vendor uses the same crate_id namespace as in manifest. If pre-burn-in shows test_pass rate <99.5% we'll still ask for 2 spares per 100.

nina: Great. Procurement-bot, mark PO 90444_amendment as pending vendor docs and route invoice expectations to finance. Track this thread for post-arrival RMA burn-in metrics and cost comparison (pre-burn-in vs airbridge).

procurement-bot: PO 90444_amendment -> draft created -> awaiting vendor test_report upload and finance approval for expedited airhold. Thread will be archived 45d after close.

maya: Thanks vendor. Once test_report is uploaded ops and I will validate sha256 and confirm whether to relax depot SLA. If anything deviates, we'll escalate and consider airbridge.

sam: Thanks team. After arrival, ops please report: actual burn-in fail count, whether spares were used, photo turnaround hours, and any customs hold duration. We'll run a quick cost vs uptime analysis.
